summary: City Council adopted the Commemorative Framework at its July 2022 meeting. The Framework provides guidance to the public, Elected Officials, and City staff regarding the commemorative naming and renaming of streets and City properties, and the consideration of proposals for new and existing commemorative monuments. The proposal to name the new long-term care home at 4610 Finch Avenue East in honour of Bernice Redmon advances the City’s broader equity and commemorative objectives by recognizing the contributions of a historically underrepresented individual, while supporting more inclusive storytelling in public spaces in alignment with the City’s Commemorative Framework. Seniors Services and Long-Term Care, in collaboration with Economic Development and Culture Division and Strategic Partnerships reviewed the application to name the property. The review concluded that the naming proposal complies with the criteria of the City of Toronto Property Naming Policy and aligns with the Guiding Principles for Commemoration, as outlined in the City of Toronto’s Commemorative Framework.
decided: The Scarborough Community Council: 1. Approved the naming of the new long-term care home at 4610 Finch Avenue East in honour of Bernice Redmon.
